what: Streets of the town where the survey draws no road line of its own (the old town and the other streets it shows only as house and wall fronts). "rings": the street surface in survey m, painted together even-odd; "edges": its edge lines in survey m, drawn in the road line; "house_trim": [x, y, rings] for each approximated house (OpenStreetMap footprint or satellite body, found by the mean of its corners x, y in survey m) that reached into a road: it is drawn as these rings instead (none = not drawn). Outside the red line only.

source: Which streets exist: the street bands of the Basemap street cache (OpenStreetMap streets of kit/Data/bergama_osm.osm, 2026-11-13 08:42:23).
Where their edges can be: the survey's own lines in the Basemap cache (closed building outlines, building lines, walls, road lines).

Cross-check: Esri World Imagery, Maxar capture of 1 Mar 2023 (library/satellite_2026-11-06), looked at for the whole frame; the streets lie on the streets of the image to its stated accuracy of about 5 m.
method: Only where no surveyed road surface (kit/Data/roads_survey.json) lies within 3 m, and outside the red line.
The free street = the street band less everything within 0.3 m of a surveyed building line or wall; a single survey line across a street (gap up to 3 m) does not end it.

Each street is a ribbon on the middle line of its free band. Half width = the smaller of (distance to the band edge) and (clearance to the nearest surveyed building line minus an inset); inset = half the clearance, at least 0.3 m and at most 1.5 m (walls: 1.0 m less). So a street keeps up to 1.5 m off the surveyed house fronts and a narrow lane keeps half of its free width. Half width smoothed along the street (lowest value within 2.5 m, then the mean over 2.5 m), never under 0.5 m, never over 5 m.
Side stubs under 8 m with a free end are dropped; pieces under 30 m2, or under 25 m long that touch no surveyed road and not the frame, are dropped.

Edge lines: the outline of the surface except within 1 m of a surveyed road surface (the street runs on into it), within 0.9 m of a survey road line (that line is the edge), along the red line and along the frame.

Houses that are themselves approximations (OpenStreetMap footprints, satellite bodies) are cut back to 1 m from every road surface (surveyed and these); parts under 10 m2 are dropped. Surveyed building outlines are never changed.
limits: These edges are NOT surveyed: they are placed between the surveyed fronts along streets that OpenStreetMap names, and are drawn in the same line as the survey's road lines so the context reads as one. Street widths are therefore narrower than the real lanes by the inset. Where the free width between survey lines is under about 1.3 m the street is drawn 1 m wide (944 m of street). Squares and yards are drawn as streets at most 10 m wide. Inside the red line nothing is added.
